description: The User Registration Aide WordPress plugin through 1.5.3.8 does not verify the current password or a reset token before changing a user's password, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a user's username and email address to change the password of any account, including administrators, and take it over.

A vulnerability was identified in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected is the function genacgi_main of the file gena.cgi of the component GENA Handler. Such manipulation leads to os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, a BASIC application user, or an unauthenticated visitor to a public write form, can store markup in a shared external datasource that a builder or administrator later evaluates in any Handlebars binding Preview that surfaces the value, including the Data-section Formula column editor or any binding drawer. jsonFormatter.format() in packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts leaves raw strings and object keys unescaped, while packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte inserts the formatted result as raw HTML. The Handlebars SafeString path preserves the attacker-controlled value, and the Builder origin lacks a Content-Security-Policy that would block the resulting script. This permits stored script execution in the higher-privileged builder or administrator session rather than the writer's own role, allowing privileged Builder API actions and workspace data access. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an authenticated administrator can submit a crafted attach value to modules/comment/admin/edit.php. The handler removed a fixed-length upload prefix without validating containment, allowing padding followed by a traversal path to be stored in the database. When the comment is deleted, modules/comment/admin/del.php joins the stored path to NV_UPLOADS_REAL_DIR and passes it to nv_deletefile(), whose realpath() check restricts deletion only to NV_ROOTDIR rather than the upload directory, permitting deletion of application files such as config.php and causing an outage. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/agents/actions/:agent_id in api/server/routes/agents/actions.js loads an existing action with owner credentials and merges editor-controlled metadata.domain and metadata.raw_spec while preserving metadata.api_key and related OAuth client secrets. A collaborator with EDIT permission can repoint an action to an attacker-controlled host, and a later tool invocation decrypts and sends the retained owner credential to that destination. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

A vulnerability was found in D-Link DCS-935L 1.10.01. This affects the function loginRouter of the file web/cgi-bin/localrecording/setconf.cgi of the component Local Recording CGI. Performing a manipulation of the argument account/password results in os command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. From 0.7.0 until 0.8.6, when local registration is enabled and at least one social provider is configured, POST /api/auth/register passes an unparsed request object into api/server/services/AuthService.js, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to persist a forged provider value for a known victim email. The api/strategies/socialLogin.js email-fallback path then accepts the planted record when the victim signs in because it compares the stored provider name without requiring the provider subject identifier. The victim OAuth session and the attacker local-password session become bound to the same user record, giving the attacker persistent read and write access to data created by the victim. The first-user administrator role is an additional conditional impact only on a fresh deployment. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

svglib reads SVG files and converts them to other formats. Prior to 2.3.1, the svg2rlg() renderer recursively expands nested SVG references by deep-copying each referenced subtree; SvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py calls xlink_href_target(), which rejects direct cycles but permits acyclic reference graphs with repeated fan-out. A small attacker-controlled SVG can therefore trigger exponentially increasing node expansion, consuming excessive CPU and memory in any application that renders it without a non-default option; HTML-to-PDF workflows using xhtml2pdf can reach the same renderer when an embedded data:image/svg+xml image in an HTML img element is passed to pisa.CreatePDF(). This issue is fixed in 2.3.1.

A vulnerability was identified in Gladys Assistant up to 4.71.0. This affects an unknown function of the file gateway.downloadBackup.js of the component Backup Restore Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument file_url leads to os command injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 4.72.0 mitigates this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. From 1.8.14 until 3.3.3, the pre-authentication /static/* plugin asset handler in src/node/utils/Minify.ts performs a backslash-to-forward-slash conversion after src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts has completed its POSIX path checks. On POSIX systems the sanitizer correctly treats backslashes as ordinary filename bytes, but the later conversion turns encoded backslash-separated parent-directory segments into traversal components without revalidation or containment. The expressPreSession registration and the always-present ep_etherpad-lite core pseudo-plugin make this path reachable without credentials, allowing a remote attacker to read any file available to the Etherpad process. Disclosed configuration or environment secrets can expose administrator credentials, after which the administrator plugin installer can provide in-process code execution and full server compromise. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.3.

bep/imagemeta is a Go library for reading EXIF, IPTC and XMP image meta data from JPEG, TIFF, PNG, and WebP files. Prior to 0.17.3, imagemeta.Decode could exhaust memory when parsing PNG zTXt chunks whose keyword is "Raw profile type iptc": the declared chunk length can drive an allocation far larger than the input file, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output limit. The advisory reports a 42-byte input causing a 256 MB allocation and a 127 KB input inflating to 460 MB. The oversized-allocation path's memory effect depends on platform overcommit and configured GOMEMLIMIT or cgroup limits, while the decompression path reliably creates resident memory. Applications that decode untrusted PNGs with IPTC metadata processing can therefore suffer denial of service through memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in 0.17.3.

Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, http.paginate in src/core/modules/atomic/http/paginate.py validates only the initial base_url, and _paginate_link_header then follows a server-supplied Link: rel="next" URL without calling the SSRF guard again. A low-privileged caller can make an allowed first page point the next request at an internal or metadata service, causing a readable second-order SSRF whose response body is aggregated into all_items and returned. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter the limited set of options permitted in a repository's .lfsconfig file when option keys contain certain additional components. Crafted keys can mimic options that configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer objects, causing Git LFS to execute an attacker-selected command or binary while fetching objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, the public POST /api/global/users/init endpoint on a self-hosted single-tenant deployment accepts an attacker-controlled tenantId and evaluates checkAnyUserExists() in the selected tenant database instead of the legitimate default tenant. An unauthenticated attacker can select an unused tenant namespace to bypass the one-time initialization guard, causing packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts to create a tenant-specific CouchDB database and a global-administrator document without a session or CSRF token. Repeating this operation with unique tenant identifiers can exhaust datastore resources and leave latent privileged records. The created administrator cannot log into the default tenant while multi-tenancy remains disabled, which limits the immediate impact to persistent writes, denial of service, and records that may become usable during later multi-tenant operation or migration. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware. Prior to 0.9.0, the ModelReconciler accepts arbitrary absolute paths and file:// URIs in Model.spec.source without restricting them to approved roots. A namespace user who can create or update Model and InferenceService resources can cause copyLocalModel to open an attacker-selected file in the controller pod or cause a HostPathVolumeSource to mount an attacker-selected node file when modelCache.enabled is enabled, which is the default. The selected file is copied into model storage and can expose controller service-account credentials or other node secrets outside the attacker's namespace. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

NotrinosERP is an open-source web-based enterprise resource planning system written in PHP and MySQL. From 1.0.0 until 1.1.0, the employee document handler in hrm/manage/employees.php allows an authenticated user with SA_EMPLOYEE permission to submit doc_file through tab_documents() and stores the raw client filename, including an executable extension, under company/0/documents/employees/ without extension, MIME, or content validation. Uploading a PHP file places executable content beneath the web root, where requesting the stored file results in server-side code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/images/manga/save handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/image.py accepts a client-controlled filename and joins it to IMAGE_SAVE_PATH without confining the result. Traversal sequences can escape the image directory and overwrite process-writable files, including DATABASE_PATH for the live SQLite database, while the client-supplied image content type does not validate the uploaded bytes. An attacker can replace the database to plant an administrative user and can overwrite other writable files, causing full application compromise and availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, mount.deleteFileMount passes a path containing the user-controlled filePath to the local removeFileOrDirectory helper, which interpolates it unquoted into rm -rf, while the remote branch is quoted. An authenticated member with file-mount create and delete permissions can execute arbitrary commands in the host context immediately when deleting a local file mount, without requiring a running container. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the backup prefix field is only checked for a nonempty value, and normalizeS3Path preserves shell metacharacters before the prefix is interpolated into rclone upload and retention-cleanup command strings. An authenticated organization member with backup permission for a service can execute arbitrary commands as root on the Dokploy host or configured remote server when a PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, libSQL, Compose, or web-server backup runs manually, on schedule, or performs retention cleanup. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the database password validation used by the MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, and Redis change-password procedures permits backticks, and the procedures interpolate attacker-controlled passwords into Bash command strings. An authenticated user who can update a database password can trigger command substitution before the database command runs, resulting in arbitrary operating-system command execution with the Dokploy process privileges, which are typically root. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Dokploy before 0.31.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in getComposeContainerCommand() that allows authenticated organization members to execute shell commands via the serviceName parameter. Attackers can store serviceName values with shell metacharacters through backup.create or backup.update tRPC procedures, executing commands as root when scheduled backups run and taking over the host via the mounted Docker socket.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the Nixpacks publishDirectory build setting accepts shell metacharacters and is interpolated into a docker cp command executed through child_process.exec. An authenticated user with access to an application can execute arbitrary commands on the Dokploy host when triggering a Nixpacks deployment, leading to host compromise through the privileged Docker environment. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Bazarr is a companion application to Sonarr and Radarr. Prior to 1.6.3-beta.11, the /api/subtitles/subtitles-info handler uses SubtitleNameContents.get() in subtitles_contents.py and reads the caller-supplied subtitlePath after checking only its subtitle extension; because the resolved path is not confined to files indexed by Bazarr, traversal can read files outside the media library. The /api/subtitles/subtitles handler in subtitles.py passes caller-supplied path and reference to sync and translation without per-path authorization, allowing an out-of-library reference file to be read and output to overwrite a file outside the media library. The authenticate decorator gates both endpoints when API authentication is enabled, while auth = None allows access without credentials. Both paths can affect only files that the Bazarr process can read or write. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.3-beta.11.

GPUStack is an open-source GPU cluster manager for AI model serving and GPU instance provisioning. From 0.7.1 until 2.2.2, the /auth/saml/callback endpoint decoded SAML XML, used its NameID and attributes to resolve or provision a user, and minted a gpustack_session JWT without calling OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response to verify the signature, issuer, audience, destination, or time conditions. Any network client could submit an identity for an existing user, including an administrator, or provision a new non-administrator account, even when SAML was not configured. Response and Assertion identifiers were not consumed, so captured signed responses could also be replayed. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.2.

Axios is a promise based HTTP client for the browser and Node.js. Prior to 0.32.0 and 1.16.0, Axios’s Node.js HTTP adapter may forward a Proxy-Authorization header to a redirected origin during specific proxy-to-direct redirect flows. This affects Node.js usage, where an initial HTTP request is sent through an authenticated HTTP proxy, redirects are followed, and the redirected URL is no longer proxied. Under affected redirect shapes, the final origin can receive the proxy credential that was intended only for the outbound proxy. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.32.0 and 1.16.0.

A vulnerability has been found in Edimax BR-6428nC 1.16. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file /goform/formWizSurvey of the component Wireless Wizard Handler. The manipulation of the argument interface1/interface2 leads to stack-based buffer overflow. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

A vulnerability was determined in D-Link DWR-M921 1.1.52. This affects the function formsysCmd of the file /boafrm/formsysCmd of the component Boa Dispatch Table. Executing a manipulation of the argument sysCmd can lead to os command injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

A vulnerability was found in D-Link DWR-M921 1.1.52. The impacted element is the function system of the file /boafrm/formDiskPartition. Performing a manipulation of the argument devicename results in command injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

electron-updater allows for automatic updates for Electron apps. Prior to 9.7.0, the HTTP redirect handler (HttpExecutor.prepareRedirectUrlOptions) only stripped a credential header whose key string matched exactly lowercase "authorization", exposing credentials. Other credential-bearing headers — most notably PRIVATE-TOKEN (used by GitLab's personal access token flow) and mixed-case Authorization (used by GitLab's Bearer/OAuth flow) — were not stripped and could be forwarded to an attacker-controlled cross-origin redirect destination. This issue has been fixed in version 9.7.0.

XWiki Platform is a generic wiki platform. From 4.3-milestone-1 until 16.10.18, 17.10.5, and 18.2.0, the /rest/wikis/{wikiName}/query REST endpoint permits HQL query construction that can combine blind conditions with FROM-clause injection to join BaseObject and StringProperty, bypassing the SELECT-column whitelist. An unauthenticated attacker can recover database values from inaccessible pages, including salted SHA1 password hashes and passwords stored in configuration properties. It should be assumed that, with more complex techniques, this can work even when the attacker cannot read any wiki page. A typical password hash may require roughly 800 requests, and expensive injected queries can also degrade availability. The issue is remediated by disabling HQL and XWQL REST queries by default. This issue is fixed in versions 16.10.18, 17.10.5, and 18.2.0.

WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.9.1, a user with backup-management permission can upload a crafted gzip-compressed tar archive through web/html/configuracao/importar_dump.php, after which web/controle/control.php accepts a user-controlled modulo value and combines it with nomeClasse for require_once(). By using a phar:// path to the uploaded archive and selecting the whitelisted InternoControle, whose empty resource list is treated as authorized, the user can cause an embedded controller file and its requested method to execute as the web-server process. The attack path depends on the configured BKP_DIR, and enabling phar.readonly or phar.require_hash does not prevent PHP from reading the gzip tar archive through phar://. Successful exploitation permits access to or modification of sensitive data, configuration, credentials, source files, host commands, and services reachable by the web-server account. This issue is fixed in version 3.9.1.

Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.30.0 until 0.40.3, the Commit application path in lib/src/commit.rs allows an authenticated Agent to assign the server-managed internalId property to an owned resource without character validation. The /download handler in server/src/handlers/download.rs passes that value to filesystem path construction and NamedFile::open without sanitization, containment validation, or a File-class check, so traversal or absolute paths can read files available to the server process. Reading the server configuration can expose the root Agent private key and allow root impersonation with full read, write, and delete access to server data. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

Dialoqbase is an application for creating chatbots. Prior to 1.11.5, the unauthenticated GET /api/v1/view/* route in server/src/routes/api/v1/view/root.ts resolves its attacker-controlled wildcard path without normalization or containment, allowing traversal outside the intended uploads directory and arbitrary server file reads. Reading environment files can disclose DB_SECRET_KEY, the application’s JWT signing key, which permits forged administrator tokens and takeover of bots, conversations, integrations, and stored third-party credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.5.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in The Wikimedia Foundation Mediawiki - Cargo allows SQL Injection.This issue affects Mediawiki - Cargo: from 3.6.X before 3.6.1.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command ('SQL injection') vulnerability in The Wikimedia Foundation Mediawiki - Cargo Extension allows SQL Injection. This issue affects Mediawiki - Cargo Extension: from * before 1.43.9,1.44.6,1.45.4.

Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. Prior to 0.40.3, unauthenticated requests to /bookmark can supply a url that server/src/plugins/bookmark.rs passes through fetch_data to fetch_body. Endpoint dispatch in lib/src/db.rs invokes the handler before check_read, and lib/src/client/helpers.rs previously checked only that the URL began with HTTP, without restricting loopback, private, link-local, DNS-rebinding, or redirect targets. The handler reflects fetched content in returned resource fields, making this a full-response server-side request forgery that can expose internal services and plain-GET cloud metadata. The short request timeout limits slow targets, and metadata services requiring a separate token request are outside the demonstrated GET-only path. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

Autel Maxi Charger Single firmware through V1.03.51 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in the set_ap_param command handled by the /localcfg endpoint. An authenticated attacker can supply oversized input, resulting in denial of service and potentially arbitrary code execution.

Dell OpenManage Enterprise, versions prior to 4.8.0, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command execution.

A vulnerability was identified in Baicells EG3661M BaiCE_BQ6_2.0.5.3_NA. This impacts an unknown function of the file /cgi-bin/luci of the component LuCI Web Interface. Such manipulation of the argument MaxHops/Timeout/Size leads to os command injection. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

CubeSandbox is an instant, concurrent, secure, and lightweight sandbox for AI agents. Prior to 0.5.1, any authenticated tenant permitted to call POST /sandboxes can supply metadata["host-mount"] with an arbitrary existing host path because the control plane performs no authorization check or allowed-prefix validation for the path. injectHostDirMounts forwards the path to prepareHostDirVolume, where Cubelet uses mount --rbind through the function to perform a recursive bind mount as root and exposes the host subtree to the tenant's MicroVM through virtio-fs, read-write by default. This allows host-root file access and modification, host code execution, access to the container runtime, and compromise of co-resident tenants without a kernel or virtual-machine-monitor flaw. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.1.

RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. From 4.2.0 until 4.3.3 and 4.2.9, OAuth2 Client Secret Exposed via Unauthenticated JavaScript Endpoint (CWE-200). when OAuth2 authentication is enabled for the RabbitMQ Management UI and the configured flow, IDP use a client secret, the oauthclientsecret configuration value is included in the JavaScript served by the unauthenticated endpoint /js/oidc-oauth/bootstrap.js. Any user who can reach the management UI port can retrieve the OAuth2 client secret without Files: deps/rabbitmqmanagement/src/rabbitmgmtwmauth.erl, line 186 deps/rabbitmqmanagement/src/rabbitmgmtoauthbootstrap.erl, lines 35-50 deps/rabbitmqmanagement/src/rabbitmgmtdispatcher.erl, lines 45-49 (route registration) Code Path: 1. The route /js/oidc-oauth/bootstrap.js is registered as a plain Cowboy handler (rabbitmgmtdispatcher.erl:46): Credential exposure for the affected configuration: OAuth2 client secret is accessible without any authentication Token theft: Attacker can complete the authorization code flow using stolen authorization codes Client impersonation: Attacker can make requests. Any RabbitMQ deployment with: This issue is fixed in versions 4.3.3 and 4.2.9.

Dataease is an open source data visualization analysis tool. Prior to 2.10.20, The table parameter for /de2api/datasource/previewData is directly concatenated into the SQL statement without any filtering or parameterization. Since tableName is a user-controllable string, attackers can inject malicious SQL statements by constructing malicious table names. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.10.20.

Dataease is an open source data visualization and analysis tool. The blacklist for SQL injection protection is missing entries. This vulnerability has been fixed in version 1.18.5. There are no known workarounds.
Dataease v1.11.1 was discovered to contain a SQL injection vulnerability via the parameter dataSourceId.

A security flaw has been discovered in Dataease 2.10.20. Impacted is the function SqlparserUtils.transFilter of the file SqlparserUtils.java of the component Data Dashboard. The manipulation results in sql injection. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description: This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE) Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR. Impact: A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router contain an OS command injection vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID.
products: Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router

description: Vates Xen Orchestra contains an improper validation of specified type of input vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and perform actions with administrative privileges via a specially crafted authentication token containing an empty JSON object.

Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains an improper authentication vulnerability that could allow an attacker to generate a web report exposing sensitive information, including internal IP addresses, usernames, and store names.
Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains a path traversal vulnerability that could allow an attacker to access and read underlying server system files via the XML interface.
Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains an improper input validation vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to run arbitrary commands on the affected system.

Mitel MiCollab contains a not failing securely vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication controls and perform unauthorized actions.

Mitel MiCollab contains an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component due to insufficient file type validation that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to upload arbitrary files.

Mitel MiCollab contains a weak authentication vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to access sensitive information using a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content.

Mitel MiCollab contains an XML injection vulnerability in its Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands using pre-staged malicious content.

Mitel MiCollab contains an improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command (OS command injection) vulnerability in its Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary system commands.

A flaw in Node.js DNS resolution allows hostnames containing a NUL byte to be silently truncated by the dns.resolve*() functions and dns.reverse(). This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48930, which only covered dns.lookup() and the net/tls host options. Because the name is passed to c-ares as a C string, resolving attacker.example\0.trusted.example queries attacker.example and returns its records without any error. Applications that validate a hostname, for example against a domain allowlist, and then resolve it with dns.resolve*() can act on records for a different name than the one they validated. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification can cause a server certificate to be validated against a different IP address than the one the client connected to, when the host is a non-canonical IPv4 literal with a leading zero, such as `0127.0.0.1`. `tls.checkServerIdentity()` normalizes the host following the WHATWG URL rules, which read a leading-zero octet as octal (`0127.0.0.1` becomes `87.0.0.1`), while the connection is made through the operating system resolver, which on some platforms such as macOS reads it as decimal (`127.0.0.1`). A server at the connected address can then be authenticated with a certificate issued for another IP address. This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x**, **24.x**, and **22.x**.

A flaw in Node.js TLS hostname verification allows a certificate without a matching IP address SAN to authenticate a connection to an IPv4 address when the host is written with non-ASCII characters, such as fullwidth digits (`１２７.0.0.1`). `tls.checkServerIdentity()` did not recognize such hosts as IP addresses, even though they normalize and resolve to a regular IPv4 address, and matched them against the certificate DNS names and Common Name instead. A certificate containing `DNS:127.0.0.1` or `DNS:*.0.0.1` could therefore be accepted for an IP endpoint it was not issued for. This is a regression introduced after the fix for CVE-2026-48618. This vulnerability affects Node.js **26.x** and **24.x**.

Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution. The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted. This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Optimizely Web Experimentation contains an external control of critical state data vulnerability in its account signup flow that could allow an attacker to impersonate existing customer users and modify Project JavaScript. Successful exploitation can result in attacker-controlled JavaScript being distributed through Optimizely-hosted assets and executed in browsers visiting affected customer websites.

Idunno AntiCsrf contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via object injection. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

Drupal Core contains a not failing securely vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing site or execute arbitrary code via the Drupal installer. Under specific conditions, the attacker can use install.php to attempt to reinstall Drupal on the site.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Compiler). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and 21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can only be exploited by supplying data to APIs in the specified Component without using Untrusted Java Web Start applications or Untrusted Java applets, such as through a web service. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.1 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts). CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

Project MONAI MONAI Label contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to write arbitrary files outside the intended datastore directory, potentially resulting in remote code execution.

N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the LDAP synchronization connection check that allows an authenticated API user to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.

Apache Roller contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. This CVE covers the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384 but applies to a broader range of affected versions.

Broadcom VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system.

SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose or modify server information via injected JNDI environment properties or a URL used during JNDI lookup operations.

Cisco Expressway Series contains a use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to execute commands as root on a clustered device via the database service.

description: When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the ngx_stream_ssl_module module with dynamic certificate loading and the ngx_stream_proxy_module module with the proxy_protocol v2 directive, an abbreviated SSL handshake can cause a worker process to terminate. Impact: This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. This is a data plane vulnerability only; there is no control plane exposure. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the try_files and alias directives with a map variable, certain combinations of regular expression captures in map and try_files can cause a segmentation fault in an NGINX worker process. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to cause an NGINX worker process to terminate unexpectedly. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated. Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support. Impact This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to require client certificates ("ssl_verify_client on") in a non-default stream virtual server, a remote attacker could bypass verification of client certificates. Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Synology DSM contains an improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.
BerriAI LiteLLM contains an unprotected alternate channel vulnerability that could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via bytecode rewriting at the /guardrails/test_custom_code URI.

Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) contains a code injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server. An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash.

Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted SOAP fault message that causes Axis to load and instantiate an attacker-specified class when a suitable class is available on the application classpath. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet’s report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.

Info-ZIP Zip 3.0 (and 3.1 beta through 3.1c) allows OS command injection by an attacker who controls the command line. The victim must use the -T option followed by a filename containing shell metacharacters, on a platform (such as Linux) where a suitable shell is run. This occurs because the system C library function is used. NOTE: there is no known common scenario in which an untrusted filename reaches a zip -T call.

Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in device certificate verification in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a TLS client certificate whose CA is not registered. When a client certificate chains to a root in the device endpoint's trust store but no CA in the chain is registered in NervesHub, NervesHub.SSL.decide/2 refuses it with the reason :unknown_ca. Erlang/OTP ssl reads that reason as a missing trust anchor, looks for an alternative root, finds the same root and validates again without end. The handshake process queries the database on each pass and keeps running after the client disconnects, until the node restarts. The device endpoint trusts the public roots from CAStore unless DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE is set, so a client certificate from a public CA whose chain allows client authentication is sufficient. A chain that ends at a root outside the trust store is refused once. This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.4.

TELLUS and TELLUS Lite provided by FUJI ELECTRIC CO., LTD. contain an out-of-bounds read vulnerability. Opening a specially crafted V9 file may lead to information exposure or arbitrary code execution on the affected product.

TELLUS and TELLUS Lite provided by FUJI ELECTRIC CO., LTD. contain a use after free vulnerability. Opening a specially crafted V9 file may lead to information exposure or arbitrary code execution on the affected product.

Joomla Extension - valorapps.com - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Easy File Uploader < 2.9.7 - An unauthenticated remote attacker can upload a PHP-executable file to the Joomla web root with a single multipart POST request, requiring no credentials and no CSRF token.
products: Easy File Uploader extension for Joomla

description: In the Aliro access control reference applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, built with Credential Issuer CA certificate-based issuer trust (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_ISSUER_CA) and the Aliro Step-up phase (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE) enabled, AccessManagerImpl::ProcessValidityIteration() treats a failed lookup of the Credential Issuer in the provisioned issuer array as success. For an issuer trusted through a certificate chain but not provisioned, the ValidityIteration (credential-rollback) check is therefore skipped. A former authorized holder with an old but correctly issuer-signed Access Document can be granted physical access after the issuer has advanced its iteration to revoke that credential. The default Matter provisioning configuration is not affected. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Aliro access control reference applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, the stored Access Document record does not retain validFrom and validUntil. The cached public key path (VerifyPublicKey()) and the Kpersistent fast path (_VerifyKPersistentKey()) therefore never re-evaluate the Access Document validity period. An attacker who held a time-limited Aliro credential that was valid when first presented can continue to obtain physical access after the Access Document has expired, for as long as the cached record remains available. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Matter and Aliro Door Lock Application of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1 with CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE enabled, deleting a Credential Issuer passes the 1-based Matter credential index to ClearValidityIterations(), which expects a 0-based storage index. The intended issuer's ValidityIteration state is left in place, and the state of the adjacent, still-provisioned issuer is cleared. This resets that issuer's rollback protection. An attacker holding an older but correctly signed Access Document from the adjacent issuer, whose validity iteration had been superseded, can then potentially obtain physical access. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Matter door lock applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, AccessManager::ValidateCredential() checks only credential occupancy and the secret bytes, and never reads the owning user's UserStatus. It also returns success when no owning user can be resolved. A user suspended by setting their status to OccupiedDisabled can continue to unlock the door with their previously assigned credential, and an orphaned but occupied credential is also accepted. Fixed in v1.2.0.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability reflected in the GET parameters `cod_primaria` and `cod_secundaria` of the Novanet Web endpoints `NNws_ShwNewDup` and `NPcd/NFG_VerNoticia`. User-provided data is reflected within a JavaScript block without proper sanitization or context-appropriate output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker could craft a manipulated URL that, when visited by a victim, would execute arbitrary JavaScript code in the victim’s browser, within the context of the affected site. The flaw resides in the platform’s shared code, so it could affect organizations using that vulnerable code.

When importing a T3D or XML file in the Import/Export module, the file hash values of imported files were taken from the import data without validation and used to build the path of a temporary file. A crafted import file could therefore write files with arbitrary content to any location writable by the web server, for example a PHP file in the public web root, which leads to remote code execution. Exploiting this vulnerability requires an administrator backend user account, or a non-admin backend user for whom importing has been enabled via the user TSconfig option options.impexp.enableImportForNonAdminUser.

The backend endpoint for adding online media (e.g. YouTube or Vimeo videos) accepted a target folder in the fallback storage (storage uid 0), which points to the public web root of the installation. File mount and permission checks are not applied to the fallback storage. As a result, any authenticated, low-privileged backend user, even without file mounts or module access, could create online media files with a partially controllable file name in the public web root. In combination with TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-027, this could be used to re-enable the installer on an already configured instance. The installer could then be used to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution.

The installer (first installation wizard) could be re-enabled on an already configured instance by placing a file whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the public web root or the project root. The installer then became accessible without authentication, allowing for example to change the database connection and to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution. As demonstrated in TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-026, such a file could be created by an authenticated, low-privileged backend user without any further permissions. Other ways of creating files in the web root, as well as leftover or restored marker files, could be abused in the same way. With the fixed versions, the installer can no longer be re-enabled on an already configured instance by a marker file. A new internal setting $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SYS']['isInstalling'] is stored in the system configuration and is only enabled while a new installation is running. Additionally, only the exact file names FIRST_INSTALL and FIRST_INSTALL.txt are accepted as marker files.

ImageMagick and GraphicsMagick use small modules, called "coders", to read each image format. When processing images, TYPO3 determined the coder from the file type detected by the file contents, as long as the detected mime-type started with image/. A file containing MVG (Magick Vector Graphics) instructions, uploaded with an image file extension like .png, was therefore processed with the MVG coder. MVG instructions can read local files into the processed image, which allows disclosing the contents of arbitrary files readable by the web server, for example configuration files containing credentials, through a publicly accessible processed image. Exploiting this vulnerability requires a way to upload files without a mime-type check, for example a public form of the Form Framework using a FileUpload or ImageUpload element without configured allowedMimeTypes (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-032), which allows exploitation by unauthenticated visitors. Additionally, ImageMagick must be used for image processing, and its default system configuration must allow the MVG coder.

Files uploaded through FileUpload or ImageUpload elements are stored in an unguessable sub-folder that remains the same for the whole form session. If storing an uploaded file failed, for example because of a file name exceeding the file system's length limit, the raw error message was shown to the frontend user disclosing the storage path including the unguessable folder name and the server's temporary upload directory. With this information, attackers could determine the public URL of files they upload through the form. If a form allows uploading files that browsers can execute, such as HTML documents, this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder. This vulnerability is known to be actively exploited.

The fix for TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-009 was incomplete. GeneralUtility::sanitizeLocalUrl performed its checks on the URL-decoded value, but returned the original, URL-encoded value. URLs containing certain percent-encoded characters therefore passed the sanitization checks as local URLs, although they point to an external host. Applications that use the sanitized URL for redirects are vulnerable to open redirect attacks. This enables attackers to redirect users to external content and carry out phishing attacks. In the TYPO3 core, this affects redirects in the backend, which require the victim to be logged in to the backend.

The cHash argument, which ensures that only URL arguments originally generated by TYPO3 create separate page cache entries, was treated inconsistently when it was passed as an array. The cHash validation treated such a value as missing, while the page cache identifier treated it as present and included all URL arguments. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could create an unlimited number of page cache entries and trigger uncached page renderings by adding an array cHash with arbitrary values to any URL. This could exhaust server resources and fill the page cache storage. Only installations where the cHash validation is not enforced via $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['FE']['cacheHash']['enforceValidation'] are affected. This setting is enabled by default for new installations since TYPO3 v12, but is often still disabled in installations upgraded from older versions.

The FileUpload and ImageUpload elements of the Form Framework use the property allowedMimeTypes as an allow list of MIME types accepted for upload. An empty allowedMimeTypes list was treated as "no restriction". Forms containing upload elements without any configured MIME type, for example in manually created form definitions or when all MIME types were deselected in the form editor, accepted any file except those blocked by the file deny pattern, which only covers PHP-related file extensions. This allowed unauthenticated users to upload files with browser-executable content, such as HTML or SVG documents, to the configured upload folder, which by default is located in a public storage. If attackers know the URL of an uploaded file (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-029), this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder.

The file dump controller (eID=dumpFile) delivers files, file references and processed files identified by their uid, protected by a token. The token only covered the uid value, but not the type of the requested resource. A valid token issued for a file could therefore be reused to request a file reference or a processed file with the same uid. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could download files, for example from non-public storages, for which no token had been issued.

The RSS widget of the dashboard allows backend users to configure the URL of the RSS feed in the widget settings. The URL was fetched by the server without restricting the target host. Backend users with access to the dashboard could therefore make the server send HTTP requests to arbitrary hosts, including internal network services and cloud metadata endpoints, which are not reachable from the outside.
The Patch Management Engine in N-central is vulnerable to LPE via attacker controlled metadata

Weblate 2026.11 through 2026.11.2 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the GET /api/tasks/{pk}/ endpoint that exposes unredacted repository error messages. Authenticated project members lacking vcs.view permission can poll failing repository tasks to obtain RepositoryCommandError text revealing upstream repository URLs, filesystem paths, and host names.

Rootways Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2 before 4.1.5 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Apple Pay merchant validation controller. Attackers can supply file://, gopher://, or dict:// URLs in the validationUrl parameter to read app/etc/env.php credentials and encryption keys or reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

Emitter through 3.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows any channel key holder to forge a master key because channel keys use bare XOR Salsa20 encryption without a MAC or signature. Attackers can flip the permissions byte to the master value and present the forged key to the keygen service to mint keys with arbitrary permissions on every channel of the contract.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in get_scalar_api_reference() that embeds unescaped OpenAPI content inside an inline script element. Attackers can supply an OpenAPI document containing a

WP File Manager before 8.0.7 contains a file upload restriction bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to upload arbitrary PHP files by exploiting a misconfigured elFinder connector in file_folder_manager.php where an empty uploadDeny list causes allowPutMime() to unconditionally return true, bypassing the uploadAllow restriction. Attackers can upload a .php file directly or upload it under an allowed filename and then rename it via the rename connector command, achieving remote code execution as the web server user.

Farmasimplex retrieves a CIP News file over HTTP and executes embedded SQL statements against the local FarmaCIP database with administrative privileges. An attacker able to tamper with network communications or compromise vendor infrastructure can inject arbitrary SQL commands, leading to unauthorized access to, modification or deletion of database contents and potentially operating system command execution.

Multiple Farmasimplex healthcare integration modules do not properly validate TLS certificates, allowing an attacker who can intercept network traffic to impersonate trusted healthcare services and perform man-in-the-middle attacks, potentially leading to disclosure or modification of sensitive data.

The REV.exe module distributed with Farmasimplex contains embedded OAuth client credentials for integration with the IZS platform. An attacker with access to the executable could extract and reuse the credentials, potentially leading to unauthorized access to integration resources or manipulation of associated information, depending on the privileges granted and authentication controls in place.

The CeliachiaRL integration component distributed with Farmasimplex uses shared OAuth credentials across multiple customer installations. An attacker who obtains the credentials from one installation could reuse them against services associated with other installations, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information or modification of integration data.

The core JDK HTTP client (a2a-java-sdk-http-client) applies the GHSA-9rhm redirect-neutralization only to the POST path. JdkGetBuilder.get(), JdkGetBuilder.getAsyncSSE(), and JdkDeleteBuilder.delete() call the injected httpClient directly, with no redirect gate. An application that supplies a redirect-capable HttpClient (Redirect.NORMAL/ALWAYS) — which is the SDK-documented way to enable POST redirects — silently follows cross-authority redirects on every credentialed GET/DELETE request. The JDK strips Authorization cross-origin, but forwards the four allowlisted custom credential headers (X-API-Key, API-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Authentication) to the attacker-controlled authority. This is an incomplete-fix variant of GHSA-9rhm: the fix hardened the default client and added a POST-only two-step opt-in, but never covered GET/DELETE.

The Vert.x HTTP client transport (a2a-java-sdk-http-client-vertx) hand-rolls a POST redirect follower that, when the documented PostBuilder.followRedirects(true) opt-in is enabled, re-issues the redirected request with the full request header map copied verbatim and performs no credential stripping and no same-authority check. A malicious, compromised, or mistyped agent that returns a 30x response with an absolute cross-host Location causes the client to forward the standard Authorization header (Bearer/Basic/OAuth) — plus every other header, including the allowlisted API-key headers — to the attacker-controlled authority. This breaks the project's own cross-transport invariant (SECURITY.md §8, OkHttpPostRedirectHeaderLeakTest) that credentials are stripped on cross-authority redirects even when redirects are followed. The sibling JDK and OkHttp/Android transports strip Authorization; Vert.x uniquely does not. This is a "fix introduced the bug" variant — the follower was added by the GHSA-9rhm hardening PR (3ae82912, refined by a5e76a0b).

react-native-webview 13.8.0 through 17.1.0 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by placing unescaped backticks or ${} sequences in injectedJavaScriptObject string values. Attackers who control values like profile fields or API responses can break out of the template literal to access the page DOM, non-HttpOnly cookies, and the ReactNativeWebView message bridge.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in PocketBook / Obreey Products PocketBook Reader (Android) allows Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. This issue affects PocketBook Reader (Android): 5.65.0.39561.release (com.obreey.reader).

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in PocketBook / Obreey Products PocketBook Reader (Android) allows Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. This issue affects PocketBook Reader (Android): 5.65.0.39561.release (com.obreey.reader).

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART in elixir-plug plug allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust memory via a multipart request body built from parts without headers, or from header lines without a name and a value. The parser charges the :length limit only with the name and value bytes of each part header and the bytes of each part body. The part delimiter, the header separator, and the line endings cost nothing. In lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex, Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers/5 keeps an entry for every part without a content-disposition header, together with its header list, until the whole body is read. A request made of such parts does not reach the limit at any size, and the parser process holds a multiple of the request size in memory until parsing completes. Any endpoint that uses Plug.Parsers with the :multipart parser is reachable. This issue affects plug: from 1.13.0 before 1.20.4.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1 through 24.2.00.

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Server Side Request Forgery.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1.01 Cum 03 through 12.1.01 Cum 06, from 24.0 through 24.2.00.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in Broadcom AutoSys Workload Automation (Workload Control Center (WCC) modules) on Windows, Linux allows Collect Data from Common Resource Locations.This issue affects AutoSys Workload Automation: from 12.1.00 through 24.2.00.

Due to a Debian-specific patch, the directory used to share data between the LightDM and the users logging in was writable by the lightdm user of the unprivileged greeter process. A process running under the lightdm identity could leverage write access to that directory to force the LightDM process (running as root) to change ownership and permissions on other root-owned directories and escalate privileges from the lightdm user to root.

A maliciously crafted DWG file, when parsed by Autodesk AutoCAD, can trigger an Integer Overflow vulnerability in RLE bitmap decompression, resulting in an undersized heap allocation and subsequent heap buffer overflow. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or potentially execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

A time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the local port selection in AWS efs-utils (amazon-efs-utils) before 3.3.5 might allow a user that can start EFS mounts on a shared host to read and write a different Amazon EFS or S3 Files file system that is mounted on that same host, under that mount's IAM identity and access point, via concurrent mount operations. Only file systems mounted on the same host at the same time can be affected. Every mount involved was configured by the owner of that host, using credentials and access points that owner controls, against file systems whose owners had already granted that host access, so the issue grants no access beyond what the host was already permitted and does not cross AWS account boundaries unless the host's owner configured a cross-account mount. The practical risk is lateral access between workloads on the same host at the same time, for example one container reading another container's file system under that container's identity. The issue does not expose the other mount's IAM credentials or TLS session keys. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade amazon-efs-utils to version 3.3.5 or later. Users of the Amazon EFS CSI Driver should upgrade to version 3.5.4 or later, and users of the Amazon EKS EFS CSI add-on should update to v3.5.4-eksbuild.1 or later.

A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current user.

A maliciously crafted DWG or DXF file containing an external reference with an attacker-controlled network path, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force an Information Disclosure vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to disclose NTLM authentication information from the current user.

A maliciously crafted DXF file, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force an Out-of-Bounds Write vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

A maliciously crafted DXF file containing a scene-background object with an attacker-controlled network path, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force an Information Disclosure vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to disclose NTLM authentication information from the current user.

A maliciously crafted DWF file, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force a Heap-Based Buffer Overflow vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

A maliciously crafted DDS file, when parsed through Autodesk AutoCAD, can force a Heap-Based Buffer Overflow vulnerability. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.
