A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

Kadence Security plugin for WordPress (better-wp-security) before 10.0.6.1 contains a brute-force protection bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade per-host login lockouts by exploiting IPv6 address handling in ITSEC_Lib::get_ip(), which keys failed-login counters on the full 128-bit IPv6 address rather than a /64 prefix. Attackers who control a routed IPv6 /64 can send each login attempt from a new address within that prefix, resetting the per-host counter each time to perform password spraying and username enumeration, and can similarly evade the auto_ban_admin immediate ban via address rotation.

Incorrect authorization in the credential loading logic in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, signed by another namespace's AWS Private CA with that namespace's stored AWS credentials, via a namespace-scoped issuer that references a credentials Secret in that namespace. To remediate this issue, users should first copy any credentials Secret they intend a namespace-scoped issuer to use into that issuer's namespace and update the issuer's secretRef.namespace to match. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

Incorrect authorization in the credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, from every AWS Private CA and certificate template reachable by the controller's own AWS identity or by any IAM role that identity can assume. This happens because a namespace-scoped issuer that supplies no credentials, or sets only a role, falls back to the controller's own identity. To remediate this issue, users should first update any namespace-scoped issuers that rely on the controller's identity to use their own credentials. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

Phoboslab pl_mpeg through commit c871f2b contains an integer underflow in plm_demux_seek() that allows attackers to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads via crafted MPEG-PS files. Attackers can supply a PES packet with payload under 6 bytes, wrapping the packet->length - 6 loop bound during force_intra seeking to crash applications.

Radicale 3.3.0 before 3.8.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inherit group-based rights by reusing group memberships never reset between requests. Attackers can send credential-less requests after a group member logs in to read and write group-shared calendar and address book collections evaluated by the from_file rights backend.

ModelScope 1.11.0 to before 1.40.1 contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability in the image-to-3D SyncDreamer pipeline that allows remote attackers to execute code via crafted model configuration. Attackers can publish a model whose syncdreamer.yaml target field makes instantiate_from_config() import and instantiate any class with controlled params, without an allowlist or trust_remote_code check, executing code when victims load it.

ioBroker.lovelace before 7.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the onCards() request handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read arbitrary files via unsanitized dot-dot segments. Attackers can send crafted requests to the /cards/_static_/, /hacsfiles/, or /local/custom_ui/ routes to read files including ioBroker configuration and stored credentials.

HyperFrames before 0.9.30 contains a missing Origin and Host validation vulnerability in the unauthenticated Studio API that allows malicious web pages to write project files. Attackers can send CORS-simple POST requests to /api/projects/:id/files/* or use DNS rebinding to plant package.json scripts or agent configs, leading to command execution.

CodeIgniter4 before 4.7.5 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the View Parser (system/View/Parser.php) that allows attackers to bypass auto-escaping through re-scanned substitutions. Attackers controlling one rendered value can inject Parser syntax like {other|raw} or {!other!} to emit unescaped attacker-controlled values, executing scripts in viewers' browsers.

AppFlowy-Web before 0.20.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the TextareaAutosize component that allows workspace members with edit access to inject markup by copying unescaped values into a hidden mirror via innerHTML. Attackers can store a database row title or checklist task containing an element with an event handler to execute script in browsers of users opening the row, including unauthenticated published page visitors.

Dolibarr ERP CRM before 24.0.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the Users REST API put() method that allows non-admin API users to set administrator passwords. Authenticated users with user modification and password rights can send a PUT request to the users endpoint with a chosen pass value for a SuperAdmin account and then log in as that administrator.

BZFlag bzfs before 2.4.32 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in NetHandler::tcpReceive() that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending a TCP message with a body length of exactly 1024. Attackers can overwrite the tcplen receive offset with a negative value to write controlled bytes before the buffer, crashing the server or executing commands as the bzfs user.

wishthis through 1.2.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in User::ownsWishlist() that allows authenticated users to modify other users' wishes and wishlists. Attackers can supply sequential wish_id and wishlist_id values to the wishes and wishlists API handlers to edit wishes, add wishes, or rename and delete wishlists.

Nexterm through 1.2.2-BETA contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows users with permissions.manage to gain unauthorized permissions because addGroupMember and setUserGroups lack the grantsBeyondCaller check. Attackers can add their own account to custom groups via the group membership endpoints to inherit permissions like users.impersonate and settings.backup.

Bonsai through 6.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to access admin pages because AdminAuthHandler accepts both Administrator and Editor roles. Attackers can use UsersController and DynamicConfigController to reset administrator passwords, promote accounts to Administrator, and change global settings to take over the instance.

EveryDocs Core before 1.6.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other users' records through unscoped Model.find(params[:id]) lookups in multiple controllers. Self-registered attackers can enumerate sequential ids to read, modify, or delete other users' documents and stored files, and rename or delete their folders, tags and people.

Habitat through 1.7.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CreatePostController::addAttachmentsToPost() that allows authenticated users to claim other users' unposted image uploads. Email-verified attackers can submit sequential attachmentIds when creating a post to attach another user's pending image, exposing it publicly and removing it from the uploader's post.

UrlHub before 1.20.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to create accounts via the POST /admin/user/store route because role:admin middleware only covers view and create actions. Attackers, including self-registered users, can submit a request with role=admin to create an administrator account and gain full administrative control.

ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the IAM role management API that allows authenticated tenant members to escalate privileges. Attackers holding even the lowest built-in role can call the permissions/grant-ids, permissions/grant, or bind/member routes to grant permissions or bind privileged roles, gaining tenant administrative access.

CloudPaste 1.1.0 through 1.9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain WebDAV storage credentials through the unauthenticated /api/proxy/link endpoint. Attackers who know a public share slug can retrieve the Basic Authorization header containing the WebDAV username and password, then read, modify, or delete files on the WebDAV server.
Files or directories accessible to external parties vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Starfish allows Probe System Files.
Access of resource using incompatible type ('type confusion') vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Starfish allows Input Data Manipulation.
Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') vulnerability in Samsung Open Source mTower allows Overflow Buffers.

A vulnerability has been identified in Rexroth IndraWorks. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the user’s system by parsing a manipulated file, because the file parser fails to properly sanitize the path name(s) or references embedded in the manipulated file. Exploitation requires user interaction, specifically opening a specially crafted file, which then causes the application to traverse outside the target directory and to write files in unauthorized locations, eventually enabling Remote Code Execution (RCE). This can lead to a complete compromise of the system running Rexroth IndraWorks.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry. If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to remove the volatile id. Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops its references first, the other request makes the final put through ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed memory. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd] Call Trace: __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd] ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd] ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd] ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd] ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd] Freed by task 1030: __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd] smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd] Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not one made by another holder. Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path, before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl() In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or 5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) on posix). However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() -> copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total), and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes) even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past the end of the slab buffer. Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: smb: client: stop processing a read response after a receive error cifs_read_iter_from_socket() may call cifs_reconnect() before returning an error. The reconnect path aborts pending mids and invokes their callbacks. The callback can then release the cifs_io_subrequest containing rdata. cifs_readv_receive() nevertheless continues after a negative return and may dereference rdata in cifs_readv_discard(). KASAN reports the resulting UAF: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in cifs_readv_receive Read of size 4 by task cifsd cifs_readv_receive (fs/smb/client/transport.c:1284) cifs_demultiplex_thread (fs/smb/client/connect.c:1355) kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436) ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:158) Freed by task 148: netfs_put_subrequest (fs/netfs/objects.c:267) netfs_read_collection (fs/netfs/read_collect.c:460) netfs_wait_for_in_progress (fs/netfs/misc.c:462) Return the socket error immediately, as this path did before the iterator conversion. This also avoids adding a negative length to total_read.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len handle_command_ack() bounds the decode with msg->front_alloc_len, the size of the reply buffer, instead of msg->front.iov_len, the number of bytes the monitor sent. mon_alloc_msg() routes every CEPH_MSG_MON_COMMAND_ACK to get_generic_reply(), which returns the preallocated ->reply of whichever generic request carries the same tid, so the buffer keeps its fixed size however short the reply is. An ack with hdr.front_len below sizeof(struct ceph_mon_request_header) + sizeof(u32), including 0, still passes ceph_decode_need(), and ceph_decode_32() returns four bytes that were never received: uninitialized slab memory, stale bytes of an earlier message, or bytes the peer planted by sending a reply that lands in the same buffer and is then rejected. The read stays within the allocation, so KASAN does not flag it. req->result reaches userspace through ceph_monc_do_statfs(), ceph_monc_get_version() and ceph_monc_blocklist_add(); rbd hands it back from write() on /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major, and rbd_get_client() passes it to ERR_PTR() unchecked, which faults: rbd: failed to get latest osdmap: -186318427 BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfffe9ca034 Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI RIP: 0010:do_rbd_add (drivers/block/rbd.c:7105) Call Trace: ... kernfs_fop_write_iter (fs/kernfs/file.c:345) vfs_write (fs/read_write.c:595 fs/read_write.c:687) ksys_write (fs/read_write.c:739) do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:61 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:84) entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121) Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception Use msg->front.iov_len, matching handle_subscribe_ack(), handle_statfs_reply(), handle_get_version_reply() and handle_auth_reply(). A well-formed ack has front.iov_len >= 22 and is unaffected; a short one takes the existing bad: path. This applies commit d3c32939fa0e ("libceph: bound get_version reply decode to front len") to the last decode-side use of front_alloc_len in this file.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: net: ipv4: add zero check for snd_cwnd_clamp When RTAX_CWND is locked, user is able to pass 0 into it. This could lead to writing 0 to tp->snd_cwnd, leading to a division by zero error. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: media: go7007: only set audio_enabled if go7007_snd_init() succeeded go7007_register_encoder() sets go->audio_enabled before calling go7007_snd_init() and discards its return value. go7007_snd_init() assigns go->snd_context only on success, so a failed ALSA setup leaves audio_enabled set with snd_context still NULL. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check ceph_update_snap_trace() bounds the two encoded snapid arrays that follow a struct ceph_mds_snap_realm with sizeof(u64) * (num_snaps + num_prior_parent_snaps). Both counts come straight off the wire as __le32, so the addition is evaluated in unsigned int and wraps before sizeof(u64) promotes it to size_t: an MDS sending num_snaps = 1 and num_prior_parent_snaps = 0xffffffff makes the sum zero and the check degenerates to ceph_decode_need(&p, e, 0, bad), which always passes. dup_array() then reads num_snaps * 8 bytes past the end of the message front, which ceph_msg_new2() allocates at exactly front_len bytes. An unsolicited CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_SNAP reaches this from a malicious or compromised MDS with no client-side action, as do the snaptraces carried in an MDS reply and in a cap import. Compute the length with size_add()/size_mul() so it saturates at SIZE_MAX instead of wrapping, in the style fs/ceph/mdsmap.c already uses for num_export_targets. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: fbdev: udlfb: don't rebuild the mode list while the framebuffer is in use dlfb_setup_modes() frees info->modelist with fb_destroy_modelist() and rebuilds it, but fbcon holds raw pointers into that list in fb_display[i].mode and nothing un-publishes them the way do_unregister_framebuffer() and store_modes() do with fbcon_delete_modelist(). The function does refuse to install a new mode while the framebuffer has users (dlfb->fb_count != 0), but only after the list is already destroyed. Reached from the 0666 "edid" sysfs attribute, an unprivileged write to /sys/class/graphics/fb0/edid therefore fails with -EINVAL and still leaves every fb_display[i].mode dangling; the next console switch reads the freed fb_videomode in fb_videomode_to_var(). Test fb_count before touching the list. fbcon takes a reference through fbcon_open(), so that condition covers exactly the states in which fb_display[] points into the list, and the errno returned to userspace is unchanged. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire: ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then overwrites it with the size of the "in" set. Neither is bounded by CEPH_MAX_MDS, only by m_info allocating, so a monitor announcing more ranks than the bitmap holds makes test_bit() read past the end of targets[]. The clear_bit() loop above indexes the same bitmap, though it is additionally bounded by mdsc->max_sessions. The map arrives on the monitor connection, which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode. CEPH_MAX_MDS is a protocol constant from src/mds/mdstypes.h, and the reserved inode ranges in super.h are laid out one rank apart over that span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt. Reject it where the rank space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map(). In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease parse_reply_info_lease() reads a 32-bit struct_len off the wire and only checks that many bytes are present, without requiring struct_len to cover sizeof(struct ceph_mds_reply_lease) (10 bytes). A malicious MDS can declare a shorter record and still get the pointer published: the following *p += sizeof(**lease) overshoot is undone by *p = lend, so nothing downstream rejects the reply. ceph_fill_trace() -> update_dentry_lease() then reads 10 bytes through that pointer on any lookup on a mounted CephFS, running past the end of the message front. Require the record to cover the structure, matching the sibling parse_reply_info_dir(). A conforming MDS always encodes the full 10 bytes. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow High-speed devices with out of spec 1024 byte bulk endpoints exist and are allowed by USB core, but xhci-hcd always sets packet size to 512. The exact nature of these devices isn't documented, commit fb5ee84ea72c ("USB: Accept bulk endpoints with 1024-byte maxpacket") only states that they "don't work with xHCI host controllers", whatever it means. But somebody (or a malicious device) can try, and then the driver will allocate a 512 byte bounce buffer for this endpoint and may write up to 1024 bytes into it if particular scatter-gather URBs are used, because xhci_align_td() obtains packet size from the descriptor. Fix this. As a side effect, TRBs will be aligned to the packet size chosen by the driver on all endpoints of all speeds. Alignment serves the xHC, not device, so this is fine. Only out of spec devices are affected anyway.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc() When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed, Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd. unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset); int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset; if (!dacl_offset || (dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size)) goto out; Commit beff0bc9d69b ("ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check") fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out, because it is only valid for 32-bit builds. Reproduced on 32-bit ARM with KASAN, by a client sending SMB2 SET_INFO(SEC) with dacloffset=0xfffffff8, then QUERY_INFO(SEC) on the same file: BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105) Read of size 2 at addr c2a273fa by task kworker/1:1/35 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 35 Comm: kworker/1:1 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc2+ #5 Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work Call trace: kasan_check_range from build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105) build_sec_desc from smb2_query_info (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:7676) smb2_query_info from handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:160) handle_ksmbd_work from process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3401) process_one_work from worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3473) worker_thread from kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436) Add overflow check.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners() client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner. BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140 fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners() nfsd4_exchange_id nfsd4_proc_compound nfsd_dispatch svc_process Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner list.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: udf: fix return value for non-recorded-allocated extents in udf_map_block() When someone creates a corrupted UDF filesystem where symlink contains other extent type than EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED, it can leads to a crash like: Oops: general protection fault KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access RIP: 0010:page_get_link (fs/namei.c:6503) Call Trace: vfs_readlink (fs/namei.c:6419) do_readlinkat (fs/stat.c:583) __x64_sys_readlink (fs/stat.c:605 fs/stat.c:602 fs/stat.c:602) This is because in this case udf_map_block() fails to convert return value of inode_bmap() from 1 to 0. Returned '1' propagates through udf_bread() all the way up to __page_get_link() where it ends up being treated as a folio pointer with obvious results. Move the reset to 0 line outside the if, so udf_map_block() returns either 0 or -errno, even if the extent type is not EXT_RECORDED_ALLOCATED.

External control of a file path in Amazon Deep Java Library (DJL) versions 0.7.0 through 0.38.0 might allow a remote unauthenticated third party to read arbitrary files that the library process can access. To do this, the third party supplies a crafted model archive. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.39.0 or later.

In EDB Postgres Extended Server and EDB Postgres Advanced Server versions 15 through 18 with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled, the key used to encrypt temporary files was incompletely initialized. The code applied sizeof() to a pointer to the key buffer rather than to the buffer itself, so only 8 of the intended 32 bytes were filled from a secure random source and the remaining 24 bytes kept whatever was already in memory. This reduces the guaranteed randomness of the temporary-file key from 256 bits to 64 bits. Exploiting this requires local read access to the server's temporary-file directory, and those files normally exist only while the server is running; they persist only after a crash and are removed at the next server start. Permanent data files and WAL are not affected. The issue is fixed in EDB Postgres Extended Server 15.20, 16.16, 17.12 and 18.7 and EDB Postgres Advanced Server 15.20.0, 16.16.0, 17.12.0 and 18.7.0; the server must be restarted after upgrading.

Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory in the cost report generation tool in AWS Pricing MCP Server (aws-pricing-mcp-server) before 1.0.31 might allow an actor who can influence the MCP agent to write actor controlled content to arbitrary locations outside the intended output directory via absolute paths or directory traversal sequences in the report output path. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 1.0.31 or later. Users of the deprecated awslabs.cost-analysis-mcp-server package should migrate to awslabs.aws-pricing-mcp-server version 1.0.31 or later.

Phison E12 and E18 PCIe SSD controllers contain a Secure Boot bypass vulnerability that allows a privileged local attacker to inject persistent boot-patch tuples into the unsigned, CRC-protected flash ID page read by the BootROM. By overwriting a fuse-derived RAM variable via a crafted patch entry using Phison Vendor Specific Commands, an attacker can force CRC-only firmware verification instead of signature checking, enabling an unsigned firmware image to load and creating a persistent controller-level implant that survives firmware reinstallation and operates below the host operating system.

Improper restriction of intended endpoints in the connection configuration handling of the AWS Labs Timestream for InfluxDB MCP Server (awslabs.timestream-for-influxdb-mcp-server) before 0.0.19 might allow a remote unauthenticated actor (via prompt injection) to obtain the InfluxDB API token configured on the server, sent to a crafted endpoint controlled through an InfluxDB URL introduced in the MCP client context. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.0.19 or later and rotate any InfluxDB API tokens configured for the server.

TridotsTech go1cms master branch through commit 7f68d05 and version-3 branch before commit ead8da3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the guest-whitelisted update_doc method that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify any document. Attackers can supply a doctype, name and arbitrary fields that are saved with ignore_permissions=True, altering User records to escalate privileges, take over accounts or tamper with business data.

SplitPro through 2.1.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addOrEditExpense and addOrEditCurrencyConversion tRPC mutations that allows authenticated users to assign expenses to arbitrary users. Attackers can enumerate sequential user IDs and supply them in participants or paidBy fields to fabricate debts on victims' balances, even in unseen groups.

Chyrp Lite (xenocrat/chyrp-lite) contains a missing brute-force protection vulnerability in the main_login() function that allows remote attackers to repeatedly submit login attempts against the admin account without any attempt counter, lockout, delay, or CAPTCHA enforcement. Attackers can send unlimited password guesses via POST requests to the login action until a correct credential is found, gaining full administrative control including post publishing, user management, and file uploads.

GeoPulse 1.5.0 through 2.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/places/geocoding/{id} that allows authenticated users to read other users' private locations. Attackers can enumerate sequential reverse_geocoding_location ids to retrieve other users' custom place names, city, country, coordinates and bounding boxes from their history.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFCommon::Util::ParseDataURI caused by storing the data offset in a signed char. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF file with a raw data URI whose segment starts beyond byte 127 to crash applications or leak adjacent heap memory.

littlefs through 2.11.3, when built with LFS_MIGRATE, contains a type confusion vulnerability in lfs_dir_traverse() that treats a stack lfs_diskoff struct as an lfs_attr array. Attackers can supply a crafted littlefs v1 image whose metadata is read as LFS_FROM_USERATTRS during migration, causing out-of-bounds stack reads and process crashes.

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size after a NUL byte in incr_parse. The parser appends each chunk to its buffer and compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. It treats a NUL byte as the end of the input, so a NUL within the first max_size bytes keeps it short of the limit. The buffer keeps growing, and incr_skip cannot remove the NUL. A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer can exhaust process memory regardless of max_size.

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing colon in decode_hv. Unless it is short plain ASCII, a quoted key is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key. A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag. With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth. A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str. A string is decoded through a fixed-size buffer (16 KiB in 4.04), and each time the buffer fills its contents move into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the string is then rejected for a control character, an invalid escape, malformed UTF-8 or the end of the input. A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains the decoded part of each rejected string, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

JSON::XS versions from 4.0_00 before 4.05 for Perl corrupt the incremental buffer length by chopping past its end in incr_skip after a top-level number. The incremental parser scans any run of digits, signs, dots and exponent markers as one number, but the decoder stops at the end of a valid number, so the parser keeps an offset into bytes it has not decoded. It then empties the buffer without clearing those bytes, and a later incr_parse call without new input reads them again and moves the offset past the end of the buffer. incr_skip, the documented recovery after an error, removes that many bytes and the buffer length wraps. A peer sending input such as "1-2" to an incr_parse consumer can make the next read of incr_text exit the process through perl's uncatchable out-of-memory path.

JSON::XS versions from 3.04 before 4.05 for Perl write one byte past a heap buffer when appending a one-byte chunk in incr_parse. The incremental buffer grows to one and a half times the length it must hold, with no room reserved for the terminating NUL. For an empty buffer and a one-byte chunk that request is one byte, which a buffer whose front was removed by earlier decodes can already have, so nothing is reallocated and the NUL lands one byte past the allocation. A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer, choosing how the input is split into reads, can cause a one-byte heap out-of-bounds write.

JSON::XS versions from 3.0 before 4.05 for Perl read freed stack memory when a FREEZE result's serialisation grows the Perl stack under allow_tags in encode_rv. With allow_tags, an object's FREEZE method is called in list context and each returned value is encoded through a saved Perl stack pointer. When encoding a returned value calls back into Perl, through TO_JSON under convert_blessed or another FREEZE, and that callback grows the stack, the stack is reallocated while the saved pointer still refers to the freed block. Encoding such objects reads freed memory, and encode can return undef without an error.

Pulse from 5.0.17 before 6.8.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/ai/approvals endpoints that allows authenticated viewer-level users to manage approval requests. Attackers can list pending requests to expose proposed commands and targets, and approve or deny other users' requests, altering decision and audit state.

HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached. The session id from the client's cookie reaches memcached unchanged as the cache key. A CR and LF in the session id end the cache command early, and the server reads the bytes after them as further commands.

Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to the session engine. read_session_id returns the cookie value as the session id without checking its characters, and Dancer hands it to the session engine to load the session. A remote attacker may cause path traversal or injection in a session engine that uses the id in a file path, cache command or query without checking it.

UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd contains an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability that allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority.

Check Point Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server contain an incorrect permissions assignment for critical resources vulnerability when the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.

HashiCorp Vault and Vault Enterprise are vulnerable to an issue in the integrated storage join process that may allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a new, uninitialized node to cause that node to send credentials from its server environment to an attacker-controlled server. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92735) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault's audit devices did not validate the contents of a configured audit log prefix and did not consistently enforce the server-level setting that restricts audit log prefixing. This may allow a privileged operator to inject content into audit logs, potentially leading to forged or misleading audit records. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93333) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not consistently apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to request paths that differ only by a trailing slash. This may allow an authenticated user who holds a broader delete permission on system configuration paths to disable a secrets engine, auth method, or audit device that a more specific deny rule was intended to protect. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93335) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Software installed and run as a non-privileged user may conduct improper GPU system calls through the DDK kernel module interface. Under unsupported use of the interface, a use-after-free condition may occur that can lead to kernel memory corruption, platform instability, or system reboot. The weakness occurs when software references memory after it has been released. Accessing memory after free may result in corruption of valid data structures, unexpected program behaviour, process crashes, or execution of unintended operations.

Software installed and run as a non-privileged user may conduct GPU system calls to trigger an integer overflow and allow OOB writes to GPU buffers. The integer overflow caused when mapping a GPU buffer >4GB causes corruption of array length, and can lead to kernel panics or out of bounds access.

Software installed and run as a non-privileged user may conduct improper GPU system calls to the execution of an error path that triggers an OOB read & write. An error can be triggered which causes the index of the array element to be cleaned up by the error path would be outside of the array bounds.

OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.x before 2.7.2, and the openbao-plugins LDAP and RADIUS auth plugins before 0.2.0, contain an ACL bypass in the AppRole, Cert, LDAP, and RADIUS auth methods caused by implicit path canonicalization. Authenticated attackers can request non-canonical paths for AppRole Role IDs, Cert CRLs, LDAP groups and users, or RADIUS users to evade ACL deny rules.

Dockhand before 1.0.55 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows authenticated users with stacks:create permission to read sensitive files by supplying an arbitrary composePath during stack adoption. Attackers can adopt a stack pointing to the encryption key, SQLite database, or /proc/self/environ and read it via the compose endpoint to obtain all stored credentials.

Fleet before 4.86.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory through quadratic XML canonicalization of unsigned SAML responses. Attackers can send a single crafted SAML response with deeply nested elements declaring new namespace prefixes to POST /api/v1/fleet/sso/callback, crashing the Fleet server.

A directory traversal bug was discovered when unpacking 3.0 (quilt) source packages, where the packaging tarball could contain the quilt database directory (.pc) with attacker controlled symlinks, where that in combination with patches that would fail to apply, could be used to make the code used to restore the backup files to either modify or remove the files pointed to by the attacker controlled symlinks.

PLANET GS-5220-8P2T2S (hardware version 3.0) firmware versions before 3.2412b261008 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to corrupt stack memory by submitting an oversized webstax_auth HTTP Cookie value that is copied into a fixed-size stack buffer without length validation. Attackers can send a crafted unauthenticated HTTP request with an oversized cookie to overwrite the saved return address and corrupt stack memory, leading to memory corruption and potential denial of service on the device.

Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition before 7.5.1 do not require accepted group membership when authorizing deletion of group share-rights. The DELETE /share/right/ endpoint checks for a membership matching the target group, the authenticated user, and share_admin=True, but omits accepted=True. An authenticated remote attacker who has been invited to a group with share-admin privileges, and who knows a group share-right UUID, can therefore delete that group's share-right record without accepting the invitation or after declining it. Pending invitations have accepted=None, while declined invitations retain accepted=False and the share_admin flag. Deletion revokes the group's access to the affected share and its contained secrets for all accepted group members, without deleting the underlying data or disclosing secret contents. The issue was fixed in version 7.5.1 of both editions, released on 2026-10-13.

CCC Attestation SIG attested-tls-poc through commit 731ca82 contains a time-of-check time-of-use vulnerability because Evidence is appraised only once during the TLS handshake, without post-handshake re-attestation. Attackers with local access to the attesting endpoint can alter workload code, data, configuration, or attached devices like GPUs while peers keep trusting the original Evidence.

Improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts in the WAMP-CRA (challenge-response) authentication path in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 allows remote attackers to guess user passwords via unlimited authentication attempts, because the path, in which the broker issues a challenge and the client returns an HMAC of it keyed with the user's secret, applies no account lockout or rate limiting. Affected releases enforce a password policy of at least 12 characters including upper-case, lower-case, numeric and special characters, so practical exploitation requires a reused or predictable password rather than exhaustive guessing. The WAMP-CRA authentication path is removed in 1.11.0.

The web interface in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 serves production JavaScript source maps without authentication, which allows remote attackers to obtain the complete front-end source code, including API usage and internal client logic, via requests for the source map files.

The login flow in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 applies per-account lockout on repeated failed login attempts, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (temporary lockout of targeted user accounts from the web interface, repeatable for as long as the attack continues) via repeated failed login requests for a known or guessed username. Intercom call handling is not affected.

The web interface in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 loads an integration iframe without sandboxing or origin restrictions, which allows remote attackers to present phishing content to authenticated users via a crafted frame source.

The login flow in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 returns different error responses depending on whether a submitted username exists, which allows remote attackers to enumerate valid user accounts via crafted login requests.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_core and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via a compressed Erlang external term in a gRPC message body. GRPC.Codec.Erlpack.decode/2 (grpc_core/lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex, and lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex before the package split) passes the message body to :erlang.binary_to_term/2. That function inflates a compressed term in full before it returns. The codec sets no limit on the decoded size, and its type checks run only on the decoded term. The server's max_body_size limit counts the compressed bytes of the request. A request with Content-Type: application/grpc+erlpack can therefore make the server allocate a term much larger than the request body. This issue affects grpc: from 0.4.0 before 1.0.0; grpc_core: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows a client to stall all later calls on a shared HTTP/2 connection via calls that the server refuses while their DATA frames are in flight. The stream handler grpc_stream_h (grpc_server/src/grpc_stream_h.erl) requests flow from Cowboy only for request data that has arrived. When the server refuses a call early, for example because the body exceeds max_body_size or the method is not implemented, Cowboy drops the DATA frames still in flight for that stream. Their bytes are not returned to the connection flow-control window. After enough refused calls the window is empty. No call on that connection can then send a request body, and each call waits until its deadline. Other connections are not affected. This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows an attacker to make a handler act on a resource other than the one named in the URL of an HTTP-transcoded route, via a request with a gRPC Content-Type. Only the transcoding clause of GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server.ex, and lib/grpc/server.ex before the package split) applies the route's path bindings to the request message. The Cowboy handler picks that clause from the request Content-Type, not from the route. A request to a transcoded URL with application/grpc or application/grpc-web is decoded from the body alone, so every path-bound field takes its value from the body. A gateway, proxy rule or WAF that authorizes on the URL path sees one resource while the handler receives another. This issue affects grpc: from 0.8.0 before 1.0.0; grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

OS command injection in the TFTP provisioning module of Zenitel EdgeAudioClient before 9.6.3.0, and 10.x before 10.1.3.0, on VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root via a crafted DHCP option 66 (TFTP Server Name) value supplied by a rogue DHCP server on the same network segment. The DHCP-supplied value is passed to a shell without sanitization. Devices using DHCP, the default configuration, are affected on every boot and lease renewal. The same injection is also reachable via the config_update_tftp_server and sw_update_tftp_server configuration fields by an attacker able to modify the device configuration.

Path traversal in the certificate upload endpoint (/api/certificate/upload) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to write arbitrary files as root via a crafted filename parameter in a multipart upload request when the type field is set to any value other than https_certificate. In that case, both path validation and certificate content validation are skipped. This can be escalated to arbitrary code execution as root, for example by overwriting startup scripts or planting SSH keys.

Path traversal in the certificate.deleteCertificate JSON-RPC method (POST /api/rpc) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to delete arbitrary files as root via a relative path (../) in the file_name parameter. This can be used to cause denial of service or render the device inoperable by removing critical system files, and to weaken device security by removing files such as firewall rules or certificate trust stores.

The pREST database REST API in Zenitel Connect firmware before 1.11.0 signs and verifies JWTs with the platform CA private key, which is stored on a data volume shared between containers, and sets the PostgreSQL session role from the unvalidated sub claim of each request while connected to the database as the "postgres" superuser, which allows local attackers who can read the platform CA private key from the container filesystem to execute database operations as the PostgreSQL superuser, including reading the master encryption key and password hashes, via a forged JWT with sub=postgres sent to the pREST API.

The host configuration watcher in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 applies a rsyslog configuration file written to a data volume that is shared with the hiatus application container, which allows local attackers with write access to the hiatus container filesystem to execute arbitrary OS commands as root on the host operating system via a crafted rsyslog configuration file.

OS command injection vulnerability in audio messages API in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary OS commands as root in the hiatus application container via filename parameter to the /api/system/audio_messages endpoint.

Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to occupy a BEAM scheduler indefinitely via a client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming request whose body ends inside a gRPC message. GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.read_stream/1 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy.ex, and the Cowboy adapter in grpc before the package split) asks for more data whenever the buffer does not hold a complete message. Once the request body has ended, every further read returns an empty chunk, so the buffer never changes and the function retries without end. A single 5-byte length prefix sent with END_STREAM keeps one scheduler busy for as long as the connection stays open, and repeated requests exhaust all schedulers. This issue affects grpc: from 0.3.1 before 1.0.0; grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming requests. The streaming read clause of GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.Handler.info/3 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy/handler.ex) asks Cowboy for up to 8,000,000 bytes per read and compares the running total with max_body_size only after the read returns. The gRPC length prefix of a message is not checked before the message is buffered. Each stream can therefore buffer up to one full read beyond the configured limit before it is refused, and many concurrent streams exhaust node memory. Releases before 1.0.6 apply no limit to streaming requests at all. This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

AiSOC 12.1.0 before 23.3.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to query the enrichment service through Next.js console rewrite routes. Attackers can send requests to /api/v1/enrichment/lookup or /api/v1/enrichment/bulk to retrieve threat-intelligence results and set force to true to consume commercial provider API quota.

MRBS before 1.13.0 contains an LDAP injection vulnerability in web/lib/MRBS/Auth/AuthLdap.php that interpolates unescaped login usernames into DN search and group-membership filters. Attackers with valid directory credentials outside the required group can submit crafted usernames that make the group filter always true, bypassing access restrictions.

MRBS before 1.13.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject spreadsheet formulas because the escape() function in web/report.php fails to neutralize leading formula characters. Attackers can store formulas in booking names, descriptions or custom fields that execute when privileged users open exported CSV reports, enabling data exfiltration or command execution via DDE.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge privileged actions such as administrator user creation by merging $_GET and $_POST parameters without requiring an anti-CSRF token. Attackers can craft a malicious link or auto-navigating page that issues a plain GET request, exploiting the lack of CSRF protection and SameSite=Lax cookie behavior on top-level navigations to create unauthorized administrator accounts.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private calendar data by exploiting a missing dateCrea value that causes the md5Id token to collapse to md5(calendarId.userId), both small enumerable integers. Attackers can compute valid tokens and request the misc&action=DisplayIcal endpoint with a forged md5Id to read any user's private calendar events without authentication.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to redirect users to arbitrary external URLs by manipulating the objUrl parameter in Ctrl.php's redir() function. Attackers can craft login links with objUrl set to a malicious site, causing the application to issue an HTTP 302 redirect to that external URL, which can be abused for phishing and credential theft.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to access another user's private mail by supplying a crafted reloadMailTypeId parameter to Ctrl::getCurObj() without a readRight() ownership check in CtrlMail.php. Attackers can manipulate the mail identifier value, such as reloadMailTypeId=mail-1, to retrieve the title and body of private messages belonging to other users, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive communications.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious HTML markup by controlling imported directory data or an uploaded CSV file, as values are rendered into table cell text and value attributes after only Txt::utf8Encode() with no HTML escaping in VuePersonsImportExport.php. Attackers can craft a CSV cell containing an attribute-breakout payload that is rendered verbatim and executed in the browser of the administrator performing the import, leading to arbitrary script execution in the administrative context.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can submit an error-based extractvalue payload through personsSort to leak database information, such as the MariaDB version, via the user and space listing pages.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge the shared-calendar iCal share token by deriving md5Id() from predictable fields such as object creation time, which is self-disclosed through autorDate and the iCal CREATED field. Attackers can compute the creation minute and forge the md5Id token to access and read a shared calendar's iCal feed without authorization.

A flaw was found in dnf5daemon-server. Unauthenticated D-Bus methods pass caller-controlled URL or .rpm path patterns into a root-privileged cmdline package loader that may store fetched content in a world-readable cache without size limits, or open local paths as root, allowing a local attacker to disclose privileged content and to deny service via disk exhaustion.

paicoding from commit b8206b9 through commit 903adce uses predictable credentials for accounts created via ZSXQ login, because loginByZsxq derives both the username and password solely from the member's ZSXQ number. Unauthenticated attackers can read that number from the victim's /user/{userId} profile page, compute the credentials, and log in via /login/username to take over the account.

paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in image upload because ImageServiceImpl.validateStaticImg accepts SVG files, which are then served from the site origin when local storage is used. Authenticated attackers can upload script-bearing SVG images that execute when victims view them, stealing the non-HttpOnly f-session cookie to hijack accounts.

paicoding commit 766c48b through commit 903adce contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in payment notifications, where NotifyMsgListener inserts the payer's display name unescaped and notify-system-item.html renders it via th:utext. Authenticated attackers can set a malicious display name and start a pending payment on a paid article, executing script in the author's browser when the author views notifications.

paicoding 1.0.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the ArticleRestController article detail endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to read restricted articles. Attackers can enumerate article IDs via GET /article/api/data/detail/{articleId} to retrieve full content of paid, login-only, member-only and draft articles.

paicoding 1.0.3 contains a payment bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to unlock paid articles by guessing weak payment confirmation codes. Attackers can start a payment, enumerate roughly 2000 IdUtil.genPayCode counter values, and submit the matching verifyCode to the unauthenticated callback to mark it paid.

ragent 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in RagTraceController that allows any logged-in user to view all users' RAG traces. Attackers can page through /rag/traces/runs and related node endpoints to read other users' usernames, user ids, conversation ids, questions, and per-node execution details.

Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains an improper restriction of authentication attempts vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to brute-force six-digit password reset codes via PUT /apis/user/forget-password. Attackers can request a code for a known email and submit unlimited guesses during its 300-second lifetime to set a chosen password and take over the account.

Seafile SeaDoc converter 2.0.4 before 2.0.11 and 3.0.0 before 3.0.8 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers holding a public share token to execute code. Attackers supply an absolute filename to /api/v1/confluence-to-wiki/ to extract a ZIP from download_url into the Python library path, then trigger the module's import via a file-convert request.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.11.3 contains a broken access control vulnerability in which the isAutor() function in MdlObject.php grants accessRight=3 based solely on object authorship without verifying the user still belongs to the object's space. Attackers who were previously members and authored objects can retain unauthorized read access to space objects even after being removed from the space, leading to persistent information disclosure.

Kanbanz by Softaculous plugin for WordPress before 1.0.3 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows authenticated Kanban Staff users to access and modify boards they are not members of by exploiting admin-ajax handlers that fail to call kanbanz_user_can_access_board() or per-task edit checks on attacker-supplied board_id or task_id parameters. Attackers can supply arbitrary board IDs to read sensitive task data, overwrite status columns, subtasks, and labels, inject comments, upload or delete attachments, and create tasks or set WIP limits on boards owned by other teams.

Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to letter case variants of user and group names in auth methods that treat these names as case-insensitive. This may allow an authenticated user with delegated permissions to modify a protected user or group, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-128100) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

- Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component vulnerability in Johnson Controls FX Server, Johnson Controls FX80, and Johnson Controls FX90 allows CAPEC‑17: Accessing, Modifying or Deleting Files. This issue affects FX Server: before 14.10.10 and before 14.14.1; FX80: before 14.14.10 and before 14.14.1; FX90: before 14.10.10 and before 14.14.1.

Post to Google My Business plugin for WordPress before 3.5.7 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Contributor-level privileges or higher to make the server send requests to arbitrary hosts by supplying an unvalidated mbp_post_attachment URL that reaches a raw getimagesize() call in validate_external_image_size() via the preview REST route. Attackers can exploit this to perform internal port scanning, probe internal-only services and cloud metadata endpoints, and trigger GET-based side effects on internal systems, bypassing network perimeter controls since the request originates from the web server.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, aiohttp buffers all additional connection data received while a request marked for upgrade, such as a WebSocket handshake, is being handled, without a size limit or flow control. A remote attacker can stream data behind an upgrade request to a handler that does not immediately accept or reject the upgrade and cause unbounded memory consumption. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, when the pipelined request queue is full, the pure-Python parser stores the unparsed remainder internally and also returns the same data to its caller. After a handler declines an upgrade request, the caller feeds the remainder back to the parser, causing the buffer to grow with each handled request and dispatching already-handled requests to the application again. The issue affects deployments using AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS or otherwise running without the standard C-extension wheel, and can cause excessive memory use and repeated request processing. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, aiohttp decompresses each member of a payload containing many concatenated gzip, deflate, or zstd streams by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, causing quadratic CPU use. Empty members produce no output, so client_max_size and output backpressure do not limit the work. A remote attacker can block a server event loop with a crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message, and a malicious server can similarly block a client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, the WebSocket reader continues parsing frames already received after the receive queue pauses the transport, and empty messages are not counted toward the queue size. With permessage-deflate, one read of compressed frames can add many megabytes of decompressed messages to the receive queue. A remote peer can send many small or compressed messages faster than the application consumes them and cause excessive memory use in a server or client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

A flaw was found in D-Bus. In configurations where the daemon falls back to using the Unix select() mechanism for event monitoring, it does not verify whether file descriptor numbers exceed allocated limits. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by opening a large number of concurrent connections to trigger an out-of-bounds write on the stack. This can cause the daemon to crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in dbus. A local attacker can exploit this vulnerability by connecting to an affected service, requesting a response, and stopping socket reads while keeping the connection open. Because the socket transport handles broken pipe write errors as retryable, the application enters a continuous retry loop. This can lead to excessive CPU consumption, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) for the target process.

Vault's Login MFA feature did not consistently enforce the lifetime of pending two-phase login requests. This may allow a user who previously completed the first authentication factor to complete MFA and obtain a Vault token after the pending request should have expired, including after the user's primary credential has been rotated. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92738) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.26.

A flaw was found in abrt. abrt-server trusts a client-supplied PID when creating problem dumps over abrt.socket and, running as root, copies that process's /proc data (including environ) into a dump directory owned by the connecting unprivileged user. This allows a local attacker to read environment variables and related metadata of other users' or root processes when abrtd is running.

A flaw was found in abrt. The completeness check introduced to mitigate CVE-2026-54228 and CVE-2026-54229 only verifies that a dump directory contains a "count" element, which an unprivileged user can create. This allows a local attacker to bypass the guard and again poison elements in, or seize ownership of, dump directories while privileged ABRT handlers are processing them. Related Problems2 mutating methods remain ungated by the same check.

A flaw was found in dbus when configured with the nonce-tcp transport. An unauthenticated attacker able to connect to an exposed listener can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by opening a connection and withholding the expected authentication token. Because the server processes this verification without enforcing a timeout, the stalled connection blocks the accept process and prevents legitimate clients from establishing new connections.

The HashiCorp cap JWT validation library before version 0.14.0 is vulnerable to a claims validation bypass that may cause downstream applications to make authorization decisions using claim values different from those validated. Exploitation requires attacker-controlled claims in a JWT signed by a key trusted by the application. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-19194) is fixed in cap 0.14.0.

A link-following flaw was found in the authorized_key module of the ansible.posix collection, residual to the fix for CVE-2026-11837. That fix guards only the final path component (os.chown with follow_symlinks=False and O_NOFOLLOW in _safe_open_write()). When an unprivileged local user replaces their ~/.ssh directory with a symlink to a directory they do not own, and an operator subsequently runs the authorized_key task as root (a common provisioning pattern), the module resolves its path operations through the symlink: atomic_move() writes the temporary file in the symlink target and renames it to /authorized_keys, creating or overwriting a file in the attacker-chosen directory, and os.chmod(sshdir, 0o700) follows the symlink and changes the target directory's permissions. The written file is chowned to the unprivileged user, so this is not a privilege escalation, but it allows an attacker to create or overwrite files (for example in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/, which APT reads regardless of file ownership) to cause integrity and availability impacts.

A flaw was found in the interaction between systemd-gpt-auto-generator and confidential computing guest VM images in OpenShift Sandboxed Containers (confidential peer pods). systemd-gpt-auto-generator automatically discovers and mounts GPT partitions by type GUID at boot with no user confirmation. In the confidential computing threat model, where the host/hypervisor is the adversary, a malicious host can inject partitions into the guest's virtual disk. Most critically, injecting a swap partition causes the guest kernel to page out TEE-encrypted memory to a host-controlled block device, breaking the confidentiality guarantee of the hardware TEE (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX). The PodVM images use a GPT-partitioned disk with dm-verity on the root partition. However, the roothash= kernel parameter only disables root auto-discovery — non-root partitions (swap, /home, /var, /srv, /var/tmp) are still auto-discovered and mounted. The generator is shipped unmasked in the RHEL systemd-udev subpackage, and no kernel command line parameter in the measured UKI addon disables it. Additionally, the PodVM measurement script captures PCRs 3, 9, 11, and 12, but not PCR 5 (GPT partition table), so partition table modifications are not detected by remote attestation.

A flaw was found in freeradius's Extensible Authentication Protocol Method for Subscriber Identity Module (EAP-SIM) module. When handling authentication requests, the server copies a client-supplied identity into an internal structure without properly checking its length against a fixed-size buffer. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by sending specially crafted EAP-SIM messages, triggering a stack buffer overflow that crashes the service and results in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in freeradius. An improper length validation in the EAP-FAST module allows a stack-based buffer overflow during session ticket processing. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by sending a specially crafted handshake request, causing the server process to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in cpio. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering a stack-based buffer overflow when creating archives in tar or ustar formats. When archiving files owned by users or groups with names exceeding 32 characters, cpio copies these names into fixed-size memory without verifying their length. This unbounded copy corrupts stack memory and causes the application to crash.

A flaw was found in SSSD's conversion of X.509 certificate RSA public keys to SSH keys. Missing size checks before copying RSA components into fixed-size stack buffers can cause a stack buffer overflow. An attacker able to supply a certificate with oversized RSA components that passes the configured certificate checks can cause denial of service and corrupt SSH responder memory.

A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder on builds with the JSON PAM extension enabled. A local attacker can submit a crafted authentication request containing a non-string OAuth2 code value. Missing JSON type validation leads to a NULL pointer dereference, terminating the PAM responder and disrupting SSSD-backed authentication.

A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder. A local attacker can send an authentication request without first negotiating the client protocol version. The responder dereferences a NULL protocol-version pointer and crashes, disrupting SSSD-backed authentication. Repeated crafted requests can sustain the denial of service.

A flaw was found in Foreman. An authenticated user with view_hosts privileges can retrieve rendered provisioning template content for a host via the hosts template API endpoint, disclosing sensitive data such as the host root password. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-96659, which hardened the web UI preview path but left the API host-template render path authorized for Viewer-level users.

A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::PersonalAccessTokensController, where Foreman::Controller::UserAware#find_user resolves the target account using User.find(params[:user_id]) without applying the required parent-user authorization check. An attacker with the create_personal_access_tokens permission can therefore invoke POST /api/v2/users/:user_id/personal_access_tokens with another user’s ID and create a Personal Access Token on their behalf. The resulting plaintext token is returned in the API response, while PersonalAccessToken#check_permissions_after_save only validates create_personal_access_tokens on the token and does not enforce edit_users authorization on the target user. The attacker can then use the forged token to authenticate as the victim, potentially resulting in complete account takeover, including administrator accounts.

A missing authorization check has been found in the user_mail_notifications function in mail_notifications_controller.rb of the mail notification API in the foreman package. The action returns another user's notification settings when only the generic view permission for mail notifications is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can view mail notifications can request any user id and read that user's subscription choices and stored mail search strings.

A missing authorization check has been found in the find_user function in user_aware.rb of the SSH key API in the foreman package. The create action attaches a new public key to the user id in the request without checking that the caller may edit that user. A low-privileged network attacker or user who already holds permission to create SSH keys can add their key to another user's account. That key is then stored with the victim and can be used by features that export that user's SSH keys.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. An unauthenticated client can obtain an anonymous registry token with an audience it controls, present that token to the service key rotation endpoint, and install its own approved signing key with no expiry. Registry tokens signed with that key are accepted for any repository, allowing read and write access to private images and replacement of repository tags.

A flaw was found in Quay where the robot account listing function constructs a SQL LIKE pattern from user-controlled namespace names without escaping wildcard metacharacters. An attacker who creates a namespace containing an underscore character can match and retrieve robot accounts and their decrypted authentication tokens from other tenants' namespaces, leading to cross-tenant credential theft and unauthorized image operations.

A flaw was found in pappl-retrofit. The application fails to properly sanitize user-supplied filenames when handling the upload and deletion of PostScript Printer Description (PPD) files. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this directory traversal flaw by submitting filenames containing path traversal sequences. This allows the attacker to upload or delete arbitrary files on the system, which can result in data corruption, denial of service, or arbitrary command execution.

A improper certificate validation vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.13, FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.13, FortiManager Cloud 8.0.1, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.13 may allow a MITM attacker to impersonate the radius server via a rogue RADIUS server.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0 through 8.0.2, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.8, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.13, FortiOS 7.2 all versions may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code or command via crafted packets.

A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to modify parts of the configuration on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to the lack of server-side validation of Administrator permissions. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HTTP request to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to modify descriptions of files on a specific page. To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would need valid Administrator credentials.

This vulnerability is due to the lack of server-side validation of Administrator permissions. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted HTTP request to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to modify descriptions of files on a specific page. To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would need valid Administrator credentials.
